answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds ensure that each identity incurs costs proportional to its actions, discouraging Sybil creation. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices further amplify the consequences for identity multiplication, making it irrational. In Nash equilibria of adversarial environments, any Sybil voyage incurs greater losses than gains, similar to a glacier's slow yet relentless pulse, ensuring that rational agents adhere to a single identity, proving the mechanism effective against Sybil attacks.
